chapter_theme: Pure and impure (சுத்தாஅசுத்தம்): what is truly hidden and what truly defiles are not where people look. The Lord sits a few fingers from the nose tip and within the body, yet is sought in far places; ritual impurity does not touch the disciplined, the worshipper, the fire-keeper or the knower; and true purity is the Lord's way, name and feet, while those bound to karma never learn its fruit.
structure_note: 2546 to 2550 on the hidden Lord, maya and karma and the inner search; 2551 to 2555 on impurity and purity; 2556 and 2557 contrast devotees with those deluded by karma.

2546.reading: No one knows the Lord's dwelling, between four and three finger-breadths from the tip of the nose; the great Veda that speaks of him shrinks back before it: such is its nature.
2546.nuance: The measure from the nose is a yogic placement for meditation; whether it points outward from the nose or inward is not said. கூசியிருக்கும் (shrinks, is abashed) puts the Lord beyond what scripture can say.

2547.reading: Deeds are one; the claim on the deed one intends, the karma, and the seed of earlier births: once one sees these and departs from them, what one does after enters the destruction of karma.
2547.nuance: கன்மக் கயம் is taken as karma-kshaya, the wearing out of karma. The first two lines are compressed; they may distinguish the deed, the agency claimed in it, and inherited karma. The claim is that after seeing, action no longer binds.

2548.reading: The hidden Thing is hidden because maya hides it; when maya is hidden, that Thing appears; for those able to hide maya away there is no body and no thought.
2548.nuance: The verse turns on மறை, to hide, and on மறைப்பொருள, which can also mean the Veda's meaning. Hiding the hider reverses the concealment. 'No body, no thought' is taken as freedom from the sense of being the body and mind, not their end.

2549.reading: Closing the blunt one, opening the cave and entering within, at the sign of the cool one where phlegm collects, reaching deep there, putting it outside in the fire and shutting it down is one's own strength.
2549.nuance: A technical yogic verse. மோழை, முழை (cave), கோழை (phlegm) and அனல் (fire) are traditionally read of closing the lower opening, opening the passage at the head, the cool region of the palate and the fire of kundalini, but none is fixed by the verse.

2550.reading: People wander searching everywhere in the land for the one who stirs the body, the good lord of the body, Nandi who is fragrant within the body; they do not know the meaning that stands within the body.
2550.nuance: காயம் (body) comes four times, closing every turn back on the body. கருத்து may be the meaning, the intent, or the Lord himself as the thought within. Sengalvaraya notes a parallel in Appar's Tevaram, 'I searched and found him within me'.

2551.reading: The ignorant cry 'impurity, impurity', but no one knows where impurity lies; once one knows where impurity lies, the place of impurity is itself what is impure.
2551.nuance: ஆசூசம் is ritual impurity, as from birth or death. The last line is circular; it is commonly taken to say the impurity is in the mind or in the body's bonds, not in the events people avoid. Another division of the words is possible.

2552.reading: There is no impurity for those who keep strict discipline, none for those who worship Hara, none for those who tend the sacred fire, and none for the knower of the rare Veda.
2552.nuance: The four are the disciplined (நியமத்தர்), the worshipper, the fire-ritualist and the jnani. Tirumular does not abolish ritual purity but exempts those whose practice already purifies; the fire rite itself is among them.

2553.reading: For those who stand in worship and bow, a purity bound in the whorl begins; those who stand in the pit cannot join it, and its signs cannot be seen except by those who are freed.
2553.nuance: சுழி (whorl) may be a yogic place, such as the point between the brows, or the turning of worship itself; குழி (pit) is perhaps the pit of births or of sense. கழிபட்டவர் (those who have passed out) are read as the freed.

2554.reading: The pure gem and the pure fire send out pure light; none know the root of the pure gem and pure fire; for those who know the root, the pure gem and pure fire become pure indeed.
2554.nuance: The gem and fire may be the inner light of yoga, or Siva and Shakti, or the soul and the Lord. தூர் (root, base) is a guess for தூரறிவார்; it could also be தூய் அறிவார், 'those who know purely'.

2555.reading: What is pure is the pure way he set freely, the Lord's holy name, the eight great attainments, and the word of the pure feet.
2555.nuance: வாளா (freely, without cause) recurs in every line, which the reading takes as 'what is pure of itself'. அட்டமா சித்தி are the eight great powers of yoga. தூயடிச் சொல் may be the word of the Lord's feet or the pure word of scripture.

2556.reading: Apart from the devotees who praise the grace of our father, the holy one who stands as the true Thing, others' minds are bewildered by delusion in the coiled whirl of suffering.
2556.nuance: The four lines rhyme on பொருள், அருள், சுருள், மருள் (the Real, grace, coil, delusion), setting the Real and grace against the coil and delusion of the rest.

2557.reading: They do not know what grows from karma, which is unreal; they do not see release through the knowledge of karma; they do not recite the Veda that says release is when karma leaves; the servants of karma do not know its great fruit.
2557.nuance: அசத்து (asat, the unreal) is the Siddhanta term for what does not endure. வினைஞானம் may be knowledge of karma's working or a knowledge that is itself action; the line is unclear. வினை opens every line.

links.note: The same verse appears word for word as 2071; the repetition places the search for Nandi within the body under the heading of purity as well.
725 tells how Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Lord's temple within it and began to tend it; 2550 faults those who search the land for the Lord fragrant within the body.

Both say people do not know what the body is. For the Naladiyar its truth is the stinking cart the vultures tear when life leaves it; for Tirumular it holds Nandi, fragrant within. The tension holds if the Naladiyar's verse is read as a judgement of the body itself, not only of vanity about adorning it.

The Kural sets outer purity by water against inner purity by truthfulness; Tirumular also moves purity inward but keeps ritual among its sources: discipline, worship, the fire rite and knowledge free one from ritual impurity.
Both fix a place by finger-breadths from the nose: 581 twelve below it, as a point of meditation that keeps the body; 2546 three or four from its tip, as the Lord's unknown dwelling.
Both set the Real (பொருள்) against delusion (மருள்): the Kural makes taking the unreal for the real the cause of base births; Tirumular leaves all but the Lord's devotees whirling in delusion.

source_issues: 2550 repeats 2071 almost word for word (யெங்கும் for எங்கும்).
2553 line 1: அவர்ககுச் is a misprint for அவர்க்குச்.
2554: தூரறி வாரில்லை is unclear; it may be தூர் அறிவார் (who know the root) or a corruption.
2549 is obscure throughout (மோழை, முழை, கோழை) and may be corrupt.
